The Corzerranean jet arrived at the airfield in Velnaz. Princess Kain disembarked from the aircraft, making way to her vehicle. She wore the Corzerranean black and gold commanders outfit, with several small military patches on the left side of her coat, one for each sector of Corzerran.

After a short amount of time, she arrived at the palace. She knocked twice on the large double doors.

[nation]Koranvistan[/nation][/quote]
The doors were opened by two of the palace staff, and inside stood a man and woman. They were dressed in similar uniforms, a dark olive green and black, with details and patches in a pale gold.
The woman, with glasses and hair tied back in a tight bun, wore a black trenchcoat as well. She stepped forward and offered her hand, [i]"Princess Kain, I presume?"[/i]
Only of average stature, she had a cold and imposing demeanor, with stern eyes, strong posture, and the whisper of a confident smile.

[quote=dhornaper;61251185][b][u]The Talara[/u][/b]

The Talara cut its course steadily through the Shamat-Argos straight in the dead of night. On the lower deck sat hundreds of containers, of which 50 refrigerated containers were special. Each of the 50 looked the same: blue paint, standard dimensions, barcodes crisp and easily visible. Nothing out of the ordinary.

To the crew, it was just another industrial shipment to Tirakan's growing industrial sector. "Water treatment systems", according to the manifest. The cargo, as boring to the crew as the empty sea, attracted little attention from anyone. No one questioned it.

The bosun made his rounds and sweeped a flashlight across the cargo. Making sure everything was fine before moving on, disinterested. The crew had noticed the heavy locking mechanism and extra seals on the cargo but paid it no attention or chalked it up to a vigilant manufacturer. It wouldn't be the first time they've seen a manufacturer be particularly interested in security.

The containers groaned with the ship as it traversed the waves, the sea splashing against them every now and then, and the crew passing their time in another uneventful voyage.

They had been completely duped about what they were carrying. Inside each of the 50 containers was a piece of state-of-the-art machinery covered in shock-absorbent foam and material. 96K6-SM surface-to-air missile systems, colloquially known as the Pantsir. The most advanced short-range SAM system in the world and deadly for any aircraft or drone that gets within its 40km engagement envelope. 40 launchers, two command posts, six maintenance vehicles, and two mobile power stations, all bound for Tirakan's military.

The Dhora port authorities had waved the shipment through, as they were instructed to. Every document was stamped and prepared to present the shipment as completely legal, above board, and very uninteresting.

The bureaucratic mechanisms had done their job, the crew knew and suspected nothing. It would be a very typical and boring trip to Tirakan.

[nation]Tirakan[/nation]

The Talara docked in the port of Marrin without incident in the early hours of the morning. The cargo was unloaded under military supervision and transfered to the next base: AL-AF1.
The Government of Greater Tirakan confirms that the shipment arrived safely and intact and was received by a formal military escort of the Armed Forces of Tirakan.
In conjunction with this delivery, Tirakan announces that selected Tiraki bases are now open to Dhora military personnel, with a particular invitation extended to their officers, to assist in operational training and familiarization related to the newly delivered Pantsir systems.
Further details will be communicated through official defense channels in the following days.
